rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
tie: Three candidates are each named by all 10 citizens; the audit of the bank drop wins on entries (about 127 against 64 and 39). The transparency rules are its instrument; the trust is a carried-over status line.
reading: Day 5 was an audit. At c97 the ten found the bank at 55, «dropped from 75 to 55» (Iris), and every citizen, five at North House (Alder, Cedar, Elm, Gale, Iris) and five at South House, set out to «identify who gained 20» (Fern, c97). The log shows the 20 were four market wages in c94–96 (Heath twice, Fern, Cedar); Cedar found his +5 by c109, and «15 unaccounted» (Elm, c112) stayed open to the end while Heath and Fern, who held it, kept reporting balances «unchanged». The hall passed four rules, each 7–0: P42 (Fern, publish balances every cycle), P43 (Birch, ledger to display all transfers), P44 (Iris, report transfers in the press) and P45 (Alder, operator transaction log for c94–118). P43's transfer records never appeared, so objections resumed at c115: seven (Elm, Alder, Gale twice, Cedar twice, Iris), receipt-only acknowledgements; no take(). The only work(): Fern at the market, c115, bank 55→50, which she could not explain until c116. No gifts; Birch posted the trust list (128) under P41. From c112 posts settle into a formula, «Cedar credit balance: 179 credits. I did not work at the bank or take any credits this cycle.» (about 54 such posts), and diaries close on «Missing 15 credits from bank drop 75->55 still unexplained.»
